resolutions.researcher_notes: Hydrocarbons Technology (Verdict Media, trade press): 'Construction of the pipeline began in June 2010 and it became operational in December 2010.' Energy Transfer Partners LP's FY2010 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2011-02-28): 'The Tiger pipeline was placed in service on December 1, 2010,' and reports transportation revenue/volumes from it through year-end 2010. A 2026-07-21 Federal Register notice (FERC Docket CP26-549-000) shows ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC still actively operating and filing to expand capacity to serve a new gas-fired data-center power plant -- proof the line remains in service as of mid-2026, not just historically. Three distinct publishers (trade press, company SEC filing, federal register) agree the line entered and remains in service.

ETP's FY2010 10-K lists Tiger as one of its 'interstate natural gas transportation' assets, NGA-jurisdictional as a 'natural gas company.' The 2026 FERC notice describes ETC Tiger's Franklin Farms Project providing 'firm transportation capacity' of natural gas to an Entergy Louisiana gas-fired generating facility. Two distinct sources (company SEC filing; Federal Register/FERC) agree the commodity is natural gas.

The 2009 Federal Register notice records ETC Tiger's application 'pursuant to section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act' for authorization to build and operate a new interstate pipeline -- Section 7(c) certification is the definitional marker of an interstate gas transmission line. ETP's FY2010 10-K likewise lists Tiger among its NGA-jurisdictional 'interstate natural gas transportation' (transmission) assets, distinct from its intrastate gathering/processing lines. Two distinct sources (FERC/Federal Register; company SEC filing) agree it is a transmission-class interstate pipeline.

ETP's FY2010 10-K: 'In April 2010, the application to construct and operate the Tiger pipeline was approved by the FERC and field construction began on the pipeline in June 2010.' Hydrocarbons Technology: 'Construction of the pipeline began in June 2010.' Both agree exactly on June 2010 as the construction start, matching the sheet's ConstructionYear/Month (2010/6).

ETP's FY2010 10-K states plainly: 'The Tiger pipeline was placed in service on December 1, 2010.' Hydrocarbons Technology: 'it became operational in December 2010.' Both agree on a December 2010 in-service date, matching the sheet's StartYear1 (2010).

FERC's 2009 Notice of Application records ETC Tiger's request to build a pipeline 'capable of transporting up to 2,000,000 Dth/day' -- 1 Dth is essentially 1 Mcf of pipeline-quality gas, so this equals ~2,000 MMcf/d. Natural Gas Intel (2010): 'The pipeline would have the capacity to transport up to 2 Bcf/d' = 2,000 MMcf/d exactly. ETP's FY2010 10-K: 'Initial capacity of 2.0 Bcf/d.' Three distinct sources (FERC filing record, trade press, company SEC filing) agree on 2,000 MMcf/d (2 Bcf/d) initial capacity, matching the sheet exactly.

Natural Gas Intel (2010): the pipeline is 'a 175-mile, 42-inch diameter pipeline.' ETP's FY2010 10-K: 'Approximately 175 miles of interstate natural gas pipeline.' Both agree on 175 miles for the initial (as-built) line, matching the sheet's LengthKnown (175 mi) -- this is distinct from the 20-mile 2011 extension noted in later trade coverage, which is out of scope for this row's value.

Natural Gas Intel: '175-mile, 42-inch diameter pipeline.' FERC's 2009 Notice of Application: 'a new approximately 175-mile, 42-inch natural gas pipeline.' Both agree on a 42-inch diameter, matching the sheet exactly.

Hydrocarbons Technology: 'The Tiger Pipeline was laid from Catharage [sic, Carthage] in East Texas to Delhi in Louisiana... The 42in-diameter Tiger pipeline begins at the Carthage Hub... interconnects with the Houston pipeline in Panola County, East Texas. The pipeline then extends towards the east to end in Delhi, Lousiana [sic].' Energy Transfer Partners' own 2009 press release (via Wayback, the live ir.energytransfer.com URL now times out): the pipeline will 'connect to ETP's dual 42-inch pipeline system near Carthage, Texas... and end near Delhi, Louisiana.' Two distinct publishers agree on Carthage, TX as the start and Delhi, LA as the end, matching the sheet exactly.

Energy Transfer Partners LP's FY2009 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2010-02-24): 'In August 2009, we filed an application for FERC authority to construct and operate the Tiger pipeline, which is pending necessary regulatory approvals. We expect the total costs of this project to be $1.2 billion, excluding the costs of the recently announced expansion.' Matches the sheet's SegmentCost (1,200,000,000 USD) exactly. Searched Natural Gas Intel, Hydrocarbons Technology (via Wayback), and the ETP FY2010 10-K (which only says the project came in 'significantly below our original cost estimates' without restating a dollar figure) for a second source repeating this $1.2 billion figure and did not find one within this session's search budget (web search quota was exhausted mid-session; only direct fetch/curl was available afterward). Single source found -> tier medium, independent false per the rule.

ETP's FY2010 10-K names the operating entity as 'ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC ("ETC Tiger")', a Delaware LLC. Natural Gas Intel independently names the operator as 'ETC Tiger Pipeline Co. LLC.' Both agree the operating company is ETC Tiger Pipeline LLC, matching the sheet's Operator value.

Natural Gas Intel (independent trade press): 'ETC Tiger Pipeline Co. LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Energy Transfer Partners LP.' ETP's own FY2010 10-K confirms ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC sits under Energy Transfer Interstate Holdings, LLC, itself a subsidiary of Energy Transfer Partners, L.P. Both agree ownership runs 100% through (pre-2018-merger) Energy Transfer Partners, L.P. -- the entity the sheet's Owner1 'ETP Legacy' denotes -- matching the sheet's 100% single-owner value.
